Q: Where is the wording that says the expression in the function's body is sequenced before the expression that is sequenced after the function call? A:

To use your quote from [intro.execution] p9:

Every value computation and side effect associated with a full-expression is sequenced before ...

(emphasis is mine)

The function body (#1) can be considered such side effect, and so it is guaranteed to be sequenced before #3.

Q: Untracked files that should match gitignore are showing up for git status A:

Test .gitignore with git ls-files

Rather than the fragile test with git status, the correct way to test your .gitignore (and other git ignore configs) is to use the --ignored (requires --exclude-standard or an exotic equivilant) flag of git ls-files as it will show you exactly what is ignored.

E.g.

git ls-files --exclude-standard --ignored --

See --ignored See-also --exclude-standard and perhaps see -x for ad-hoc testing while drafting a .gitconfig

Regarding the comments: .gitignore should use *nix line endings, sure, however this is unlikely your issue; Rather, an encoding might be so as @matt mentioned:

Compare stackoverflow.com/a/78319723/341994

In short: Use ascii or utf-8 for a safe choice, but I have found others work too.

TL;DR; let's explore the issue of line endings issue a bit (I used a bash shell for this example):

$ # cd /tmp
$ mkdir bad-repo
$ cd bad-repo
$ git init .
$ # create your .gitignore with CFLF line endings (windows line-endings)
$ printf '%s\r\n%s\r\n' '*.ods' 'ignoreme.odt' > .gitignore
$ head -n10 .gitignore
*.ods
ignoreme.odt
$ xxd -g1 .gitignore
00000000: 2a 2e 6f 64 73 0d 0a 69 67 6e 6f 72 65 6d 65 2e  *.ods..ignoreme.
00000010: 6f 64 74 0d 0a                                   odt..
$ # note the '0d' is not a git issue
$ echo "example" > bad.ods
$ git ls-files --exclude-standard --ignored --other
bad.ods
$ git status
On branch master

No commits yet

Untracked files:
  (use "git add <file>..." to include in what will be committed)
    .gitignore

nothing added to commit but untracked files present (use "git add" to track)
$

Q: Make Web push notification work using webview in a native android app? A:

Ow, of course this is possible! I easily implemented push web notifications from one signal in my webview App using crosswalk.

Uses crosswalk, extends Main activity to XWalkactivity Put this on on create:

OneSignal.startInit(this)
                .inFocusDisplaying(OneSignal.OSInFocusDisplayOption.Notification)
                .unsubscribeWhenNotificationsAreDisabled(true)
                .init();

Yeah, you will have web push notifications working!!!
